questionText:
Consider routing table of an organization’s router shown below:

Subnet NumberSubnet MaskNext Hop
12.20.164.0255.255.252.0R1
12.20.170.0255.255.254.0R2
12.20.168.0255.255.254.0Interface 0
12.20.166.0255.255.254.0Interface 1
defaultR3

Which of the following prefixes in CIDR notation can be collectively used to correctly aggregate all of the subnets in the routing table?
explanation:
To determine which prefixes can collectively aggregate all subnets, let's find the IP address range for each entry in the routing table:

1. Subnet Ranges:
• Entry 1: $12.20.164.0$ with mask $255.255.252.0$ ($/22$)
$\rightarrow$ IP Range: $12.20.164.0$ to $12.20.167.255$ (3rd octet: $164$–$167$)
• Entry 2: $12.20.170.0$ with mask $255.255.254.0$ ($/23$)
$\rightarrow$ IP Range: $12.20.170.0$ to $12.20.171.255$ (3rd octet: $170$–$171$)
• Entry 3: $12.20.168.0$ with mask $255.255.254.0$ ($/23$)
$\rightarrow$ IP Range: $12.20.168.0$ to $12.20.169.255$ (3rd octet: $168$–$169$)
• Entry 4: $12.20.166.0$ with mask $255.255.254.0$ ($/23$)
$\rightarrow$ IP Range: $12.20.166.0$ to $12.20.167.255$ (3rd octet: $166$–$167$)

2. Combined Range Required:
The full IP space spanned by all subnets is from $12.20.164.0$ to $12.20.171.255$ (3rd octets from $164$ to $171$).

3. Prefix Evaluation:
• $12.20.164.0/22$ (Option B): Covers range $12.20.164.0$ to $12.20.167.255$.
• $12.20.168.0/22$ (Option D): Covers range $12.20.168.0$ to $12.20.171.255$.

Together, $12.20.164.0/22$ and $12.20.168.0/22$ precisely cover the entire contiguous block of subnets ($12.20.164.0$ to $12.20.171.255$) without covering extraneous addresses.

Hence, options (B) and (D) are correct.
